headline: Bogra journalist arrested over defamatory news on State Minister
summary: Acting Editor of Daily Agrajatra Protidin is jailed following a case filed under the Cyber Security Act and extortion charges.
details: Md. Rezanur Islam, Acting Editor of Daily Agrajatra Protidin, was arrested by the Bogra District Police Detective Branch (DB) and sent to jail by the Chief Judicial Magistrate's court.
The arrest followed a case filed on Wednesday night at Bogra Sadar Police Station under the Cyber Security Act and for extortion, involving six journalists including the paper's editor.

The case was filed by Tanvir Alam, editor of the local daily Mahasthan and treasurer of the Bogra Press Club, alleging that the accused published false and misleading information to damage the reputation of State Minister Mir Shah Alam.
State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives Mir Shah Alam later issued a statement clarifying that he did not authorize or direct the filing of the case.
The Minister expressed regret over the arrest of the journalists and hoped for a peaceful resolution through mutual discussion and legal processes, calling for the journalist's quick release.
He also urged journalists to verify information neutrally before publishing news and asked the public not to take personal initiatives to file cases or make statements in his name.
caption:
A journalist is behind bars for reports on a State Minister, but the Minister himself says he didn't order the arrest.

Md. Rezanur Islam, Acting Editor of Daily Agrajatra Protidin, was arrested by the Bogra District Police Detective Branch (DB) and sent to jail by the Chief Judicial Magistrate's court.

The arrest followed a case filed on Wednesday night at Bogra Sadar Police Station under the Cyber Security Act and for extortion, involving six journalists including the paper's editor.

The case was filed by Tanvir Alam, editor of the local daily Mahasthan and treasurer of the Bogra Press Club, alleging that the accused published false and misleading information to damage the reputation of State Minister Mir Shah Alam.

State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives Mir Shah Alam later issued a statement clarifying that he did not authorize or direct the filing of the case.

The Minister expressed regret over the arrest of the journalists and hoped for a peaceful resolution through mutual discussion and legal processes, calling for the journalist's quick release.

He also urged journalists to verify information neutrally before publishing news and asked the public not to take personal initiatives to file cases or make statements in his name.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo

headline_marked: Ekushey Padak-winning [[poet Al Mujahidi dies]] at 83
headline: Ekushey Padak-winning poet Al Mujahidi dies at 83
summary: The renowned poet and recipient of the Ekushey Padak, one of Bangladesh's highest civilian awards, has passed away.
details: Ekushey Padak-winning poet Al Mujahidi has passed away. He was either 83 or 86 years old, according to different reports.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has expressed her grief and mourning over the loss of the poet.
Al Mujahidi was a highly respected figure in Bangladeshi literature, recognized for his contributions to the arts and theH arts.
His legacy as an award-winning poet continues to be his primary contribution to the literature of Bangladesh.
caption:
A legendary voice of Bangladeshi literature has fallen silent.

Ekushey Padak-winning poet Al Mujahidi has passed away. He was either 83 or 86 years old, according to different reports.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has expressed her grief and mourning over the loss of the poet.

Al Mujahidi was a highly respected figure in Bangladeshi literature, recognized for his contributions to the arts and theH arts.

His legacy as an award-winning poet continues to be his primary contribution to the literature of Bangladesh.

#AlMujahidi #Poetry #Bangladesh #Literature #EkusheyPadak

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Somoy News, The Daily Star, bdnews24.com
